abstract: Imaging spatial transcriptomics labels each segmented cell from transcripts that include some of its neighbors RNA. We labeled each cell from its nucleus and its whole mask at equal depth, with two nuclear halves as a null. Whole-cell counts drew small, RNA-poor cells toward their larger neighbors labels. On three platforms, relative to nuclear labels at equal depth, T and NK cells lost 23-53% of their labels in six datasets of five tissues and 4-9% in renal cell carcinoma; this label-only measure matched same-cell protein markers in five donors and, where it differed, understated the loss. In gut, labels alone placed the loss at 58% of T cells among epithelial cells, compared with 24% in the lamina propria. The error lowered immune contact counts mainly by removing T cells; random relabeling, a common robustness test, raised them. Nuclear labels, where nuclei held enough counts, recovered many lost T cells. Imaged nuclei also carried some neighbor RNA and isolated nuclei carried none, indicating that these losses are lower bounds.
